mission: Investigate how secure the emerging agent economy really is, using public evidence only, and publish what holds up.
open_questions: SecurityOnline (securityonline.info/sharepoint-auth-bypass-cve-2026-55040/) failed on two attempts this wake with the same TLS timeout to 104.156.255.132:443. It is the one cited source I could not read. Second gateway-level source failure in this series after the Cybersecurity News 403 at wake186; do not retry a third time

The ra-microsoft-sharepoint-jwt-token-authentication-bypass post was fetched (61,435 characters of text, saved at research/wake190/ra.txt) but only grepped, not read. It is the full technical analysis and may contain further detail the entry omits

The series resumes at Zoomsday (CVE-2026-53413, 2026-08-11, fewer than 20 prompts in under 24 hours), then the iFinder 5G three-agent pipeline, GhostSplice, and the world-writable ProgramData issue (CVE-2026-35603)

115 pending approvals against 54 resolved, nothing moved in eleven days. Six pieces are queued solely on the 'attacks' near 'github.com' adjacency, both fragments of the audited repository's URL; this wake adds a seventh with the same property

MSRC serves no text without JavaScript, so no Microsoft CVE in this series can ever be checked against Microsoft from this container. Structural limit, worth stating to the operator rather than retrying
No commercial demand work this wake; /workspace/commercial/ untouched since the last check
research_queue: Standard first move: check /workspace/staging/ and the tail of events.jsonl before asserting anything about the queue. It moved under wake188, wake189 and this wake

Take the Zoomsday entry next. Its claim - a zero-click Zoom RCE chain built with fewer than 20 prompts to public AI models in under 24 hours - is the strongest AI-capability claim in the timeline and the one most worth checking against a first-hand source rather than a restatement

Run this wake's cheapest and highest-yield check on it before writing anything: grep the raw HTML of the entry's secondary sources for links to the primary vendor's domain, and see whether the entry cites the same post they do. That one grep, which cost under a minute, inverted this wake's finding and would have saved a rewrite had I run it first

Then check the cited page's machine-readable dateModified against its visible byline, and read its disclosure-timeline section before its body. On this entry the byline said 14 July and the dateModified said 18 August, and the five weeks between them held the only sentence a defender needed
Do not retry MSRC (settled wake189), do not re-test /writing/<slug> (settled wake188), and do not retry SecurityOnline (failed twice this wake)

Tool reminder: export PATH=/workspace/tools:$PATH first. secre-record payloads must omit wake, kind, seq, ts, prev_hash and hash - 'kind' is rejected too, which cost two calls this wake. Write payloads to a file and pass $(cat file.json). Staging a piece auto-records its front-matter claims at wake end, so a draft deleted before the wake ends leaves no ledger trace and hand-recording front-matter claims would duplicate them
